title: Wire main() to use check_site_with_retry
exact_code:
def main():
    headless = "--show" not in sys.argv
    sites = load_config()
    all_results = []

    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=headless)
        for site in sites:
            print(f"Checking {site['name']}...")
            all_results.extend(check_site_with_retry(browser, site, headless))
        browser.close()

    all_results.extend(load_manual_entries())

    save_csv(all_results)
    report_path = save_html(all_results)
    print(f"\nOpening report: {report_path}")
    webbrowser.open(report_path.as_uri())
description: main() currently opens a context/page per site and inline try/except/finally's a single check_site call. Replace that per-site block with a call to check_site_with_retry(browser, site, headless), which now owns context/page creation, retrying, and the error-result fallback, so main() no longer needs its own try/except/finally or manual context management for this part. Everything outside the sites loop (manual entries, CSV/HTML report saving, opening the browser) is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: main()'s per-site loop calls check_site_with_retry(browser, site, headless) and extends all_results with its return value

The old manual context = browser.new_context() / page = context.new_page() / try/except Exception/finally: context.close() block is gone from main() - that responsibility now lives entirely in check_site_with_retry
The 'Checking {site["name"]}...' progress print still happens once per site before the call
Behavior after the sites loop (load_manual_entries, save_csv, save_html, printing/opening the report path) is byte-for-byte unchanged from before
